en.question: An MCP server runs as a local subprocess of the host application on the same machine. Which transport is the natural choice?

options.text: A WebSocket bound to a port on the host's public network interface.
options.note: Unnecessary for a local subprocess and needlessly exposes a network surface.

options.text: stdio, exchanging JSON-RPC over the subprocess's standard streams.
SMTP, queuing each request so no message can be lost in transit.
options.note: Email is not a transport for a synchronous RPC protocol.

options.text: A shared file on disk that both processes poll once every second.
options.note: File polling is slow, racy, and not part of the specification.

en.explanation: The host launches the server as a subprocess and talks over stdin and stdout, with no ports and no network exposure. Remote servers use an HTTP-based transport instead.
